## Added

- `dossier`: a `signature` check — the name a hand wrote against the identity
  document filed beside it. Two fact kinds carry it: `signatory`, the name the
  vision pass reads next to a signature on a consent statement or a
  declaration, and `identity_holder`, whom a passport or an ID card names. Both
  are person-valued and canonicalised to the same `person:` ids the owner and
  applicant facts already use, so a signature reads equal to the passport that
  names the same person however either spelled or cased it. The check is one
  per signed page, `subject` the signatory's person id: `agree` when an
  identity document filed with it names that person, `near_miss` within two
  edits, `disagree` when none of them does, and `unreadable` when the group
  files no passport or ID card at all — the paper a signature would be verified
  against is simply not there. Pairing is per group, never document-wide: a
  submission carries one consent statement per neighbour, each with its own
  passport, and measuring a signatory against a stranger's papers would be
  noise. **The strokes are never compared.** This reads names, not handwriting;
  matching a signature against a specimen is forensic work no model here can
  do, and a check that claimed it would be worse than none.

  Only a vision pass produces the two facts — the deterministic pass cannot
  read handwriting — so a dossier run without `--answers` or `--vlm` emits no
  `signature` check, and neither does the corpus as it stands: the recorded
  answers in `data/annotations/answers/` predate the prompt and carry no
  `signatory` fact. What the corpus does show is the shape the check will meet.
  Thirteen consent statements are filed across dossiers 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 13 and
  14. Eight of them — in 2, 6, 13 and 14 — sit in a group that also holds a
  passport or an ID card, so they have something to be checked against; the two
  in 3, whose ID cards are filed under `identity` alone, and the three in 7 and
  8, which file no identity document at all, would come back `unreadable`.

## Changed

- `docs/annotation-schema.md` now documents `facts[]` and `access[]` on a page
  answer, which the `dossier --answers` input already accepted but the field
  reference did not describe. `schema_version` stays 0.4.0: the container is
  not new, only the two kinds it now accepts.
- Internal: `checks::run` is handed one `PageView` per page — number, trust,
  labels and groups — instead of the two page lists the caller used to
  precompute, and projects the certificate pages and the unread official pages
  from it itself. It is what lets a check pair a signature with the papers in
  its own group. No output changes.
- Workspace version 0.15.1, which `docs/json-api.md` now describes.
  `checks[].kind` gains `signature` and `facts[].kind` gains `signatory` and
  `identity_holder`; both are additive, and nothing is renamed or removed. A
  caller that branches on either enum sees values it has not seen before.
